headings.title: Mandatory peace officer license for commission
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person from holding a commission as a peace officer without a valid peace officer license.

headings.title: Establishment of license classes and commission restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to establish peace officer license classes and provides that the director may restrict certain classes by county classification, state agency, or reserve-officer status.

headings.title: Statutory exemptions from peace officer licensing
headings.reviewNote: Exempts persons without arrest power, elected county officials (subject to chapter 57), unarmed section 64.335 park rangers, specified small political subdivision commissions in effect continuously since August 28, 2001 (excluding first-class charter counties), and grandfathered reserve (since August 15, 1988) or full-time (since December 31, 1978) officers.

headings.title: Local authority to require higher standards
headings.reviewNote: Provides that any political subdivision or law enforcement agency may require peace officers to meet standards more stringent than chapter licensure requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 590.020; verified alignment and added grandfather dates and charter-county exception in subsection 3.

headings.title: Minimum standards for basic officer training
headings.reviewNote: Requires the POST commission to establish minimum basic training standards, which may vary by license class under section 590.020(2).

headings.title: Age, citizenship, education, and examination requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to set minimum age, citizenship, and general education requirements (high school program under chapter 167 or GED) and provides the director may require a qualifying certification exam score.

headings.title: Licensure of out-of-state, federal, and military officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to provide for licensure, with or without additional basic training, of peace officers credentialed by other states or jurisdictions, including federal and military officers.

headings.title: License application procedure and issuance
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to establish an application procedure and issue the proper peace officer license when chapter requirements are met.

headings.title: Continuing education, address of record, and Rap Back enrollment
headings.reviewNote: Conditions licensure on completing POST continuing education, maintaining a current address of record, and submitting fingerprints on or before January 1, 2022 (and upon commissioning with a different agency) for FBI background checks and state/federal Rap Back enrollment.

headings.title: Five-year license expiration, relicensure, and continuing licensure
headings.reviewNote: Expires a license after five consecutive years without a commission, requires POST relicensure rules (which may require retraining), and provides the director may allow restricted continuing licensure for certain non-chapter peace officer commissions.

headings.title: Mandatory law enforcement agency Rap Back enrollment
headings.reviewNote: Requires all law enforcement agencies to enroll in state and federal Rap Back programs on or before January 1, 2022, and maintain enrollment for all commissioned officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 590.030; verified alignment and preserved mandatory/permissive distinctions and January 1, 2022 dates.

headings.title: Chief of police training course standards and deadline
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to establish minimum standards for an at-least-40-hour chief of police training course, and requires police chiefs appointed after August 28, 2023, to attend within six months of appointment.

headings.title: Exemption request based on equivalent training or experience
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a police chief may request exemption by submitting proof of completing the FBI National Academy or equivalent course within the past ten years or at least five years of Missouri police chief experience.

headings.title: Preclusion from training and grant funds for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Precludes any agency whose police chief appointed after August 28, 2023, fails to complete the course within six months from receiving POST training funds, state grants, or federal grants until completion.

headings.title: Regular compensation and optional POST fund payment
headings.reviewNote: Requires regular compensation while attending the training course and provides that course costs may be paid from the POST commission fund under section 590.178.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 590.033; corrected subsection 4 from fabricated travel reimbursement to optional POST fund payment and added the August 28, 2023 date and 40-hour/6-month timelines.

headings.title: Minimum six-hundred-hour basic training and statutory exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to set basic training at no lower than 600 hours, with six exceptions including up to 1,000 hours for state agencies, as few as 120 hours for restricted reserve officers, grandfathered 2001/2002 licenses, and recognition of out-of-state/federal/military training.

headings.title: Director authority to limit statutory training exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to limit any subsection 1 exception to persons remaining in the same commission or transferring to a commission in a similar jurisdiction.

headings.title: Mandatory thirty-hour domestic and family violence curriculum
headings.reviewNote: Requires basic training for every peace officer (except conservation agents) to include at least thirty hours of domestic and family violence investigation and management training developed in consultation with enumerated state and victim-advocacy partners.

headings.title: Six-hour racial profiling, implicit bias, and de-escalation training
headings.reviewNote: Requires basic training for officers first licensed on or after August 28, 2027, to include at least six hours covering racial profiling (two hours), implicit bias (two hours), and de-escalation (two hours).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 590.040 (2025 H.B. 495); replaced fabricated suicide-prevention heading in subsection 3 with 30-hour domestic/family violence training and corrected subsection 4 to 6 hours (racial profiling, implicit bias, and de-escalation).

headings.title: Continuing education, trafficking, and racial profiling mandates
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to set continuing education standards, mandates two hours of sex and human trafficking training per one-year period (effective January 1, 2027, expiring December 31, 2031), and mandates three hours of racial profiling training per three-year period for officers making traffic stops.

headings.title: Provider licensing, discipline, and chapter 536 appeal
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to license continuing education providers, authorizes probation, suspension, or revocation upon written notice of reasons, and grants chapter 536 appeal rights.

headings.title: Partial cost reimbursement from POST commission fund
headings.reviewNote: Provides for partial reimbursement of continuing education costs from the section 590.178 fund subject to availability, excluding persons not actively commissioned or employed by a county or municipal agency.

headings.title: Director authority to advance officer professionalism
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the director may engage in activities to further peace officer professionalism through training and education, including specialized DPS training.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 590.050 (2026 H.B. 2273, et al.); corrected subsection 1 from fabricated de-escalation/suicide topics to 2-hour trafficking (1-01-27 to 12-31-31) and 3-hour racial profiling training.

headings.title: Minimum standards for instructors, centers, and basic admittance
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to establish minimum standards for training instructors and training centers, and requires the director to establish minimum qualifications for admittance into basic training.

headings.title: Licensing and discipline of instructors, centers, and curricula
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to license training instructors, centers, and curricula, authorizes probation, suspension, or revocation upon written notice, and grants chapter 536 appeal rights.

headings.title: Fingerprint-based state and FBI background checks for applicants
headings.reviewNote: Requires basic training applicants to submit fingerprints for MSHP and FBI criminal history checks under section 43.540, with all discovered criminal history records accessible to the director notwithstanding section 610.120.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 590.060 (2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174); corrected subsection 1 admittance qualifications and added section 610.120 override in subsection 3.

headings.title: Thirty-day notification of officer commission
headings.reviewNote: Requires agency chief executive officers to notify the director within thirty days after commissioning a peace officer, and provides the director may require a current criminal history background check.

headings.title: Thirty-day notification of officer departure and circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying the director within thirty days after a licensed officer departs employment or loses commission, specifying applicable circumstances among four enumerated categories.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of officer disciplinary cause
headings.reviewNote: Requires agency chief executive officers with reasonable grounds to believe a commissioned officer is subject to discipline under section 590.080 to report that knowledge to the director.

headings.title: Absolute immunity for compliance with false-information exception
headings.reviewNote: Grants agency chief executive officers absolute immunity from suit for complying with this section unless they presented false information to the director intending to cause reputational harm to the officer.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 590.070 (2021 S.B. 53 & 60); added the intentional false-information exception to immunity in subsection 4.

headings.title: Definitions of gross misconduct, moral turpitude, and reckless disregard
headings.reviewNote: Defines gross misconduct, moral turpitude, and reckless disregard for purposes of peace officer discipline under this section.

headings.title: Nine statutory causes for peace officer discipline
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates nine causes for discipline, including lack of competency/safety, criminal offenses, moral turpitude or reckless disregard, material misrepresentation, probation/chapter violations, non-prescribed controlled substance positive tests, out-of-state revocation/suspension, and gross misconduct.

headings.title: Administrative hearing commission complaint and cause finding
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the director may file a complaint with the AHC to determine whether cause exists, prohibiting the AHC from considering severity, rehabilitation, or impinging on the director's disciplinary discretion.

headings.title: Director thirty-day disciplinary hearing and sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director, within thirty days of an AHC cause finding, to hold a hearing and probate, suspend, or permanently revoke the license, with failure to appear waiving the hearing.

headings.title: Certified mail or publication notice of hearings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes hearing notice by certified mail to the address of record (citing section 590.130(3)(2), which an archived footnote notes was repealed by 2001 H.B. 80) or by publication, with refusal or undeliverability as evidence of notice.

headings.title: Informal disposition by voluntary surrender or submission
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that a licensee may informally dispose of a disciplinary cause with the director's consent by voluntarily surrendering a license or submitting to discipline.

headings.title: Application of chapter 621 administrative procedures
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 621 and its amendments, except where conflicting with chapter 590, to AHC proceedings under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 590.080 (2023 S.B. 186); fixed subsection 1 definitions (all three terms), mandatory hearing/sanctions in subsection 4, and archived repealed-section footnote in subsection 5.

headings.title: Grounds for immediate emergency license suspension
headings.reviewNote: Establishes cause to immediately suspend a license if the licensee is indicted, charged, or convicted of a felony, subject to another jurisdiction's suspension/revocation order, or presents a clear and present danger to public health or safety.

headings.title: Ex parte emergency suspension order, service, and dissolution
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director, after filing a section 590.080 complaint and finding probable cause, to issue an emergency suspension order without notice or hearing, served by certified mail (citing repealed section 590.130(3)(2) per archived footnote) with agency notice, and to dissolve it at any time.

headings.title: Five-business-day emergency AHC hearing on probable cause
headings.reviewNote: Permits a suspended licensee to petition the AHC for an emergency probable-cause hearing within five business days (admitting sworn affidavits/depositions, barring stays without hearing, and making findings nonbinding in section 590.080 proceedings).

headings.title: Appeal of emergency suspension decision to Cole County circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any aggrieved party to appeal an AHC decision under this section to the Cole County circuit court under section 536.100.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 590.090; added out-of-state order ground in subsection 1, archived repealed-section footnote and dissolution authority in subsection 2, and nonbinding-findings rule in subsection 3.

headings.title: Cause for denial based on disciplinary grounds
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director cause to deny an application for a peace officer license or basic training entrance when the director has knowledge that would constitute cause to discipline a licensee.

headings.title: Cause for denial based on prior revocation or surrender
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director cause to deny a license or basic training application when the applicant previously had a peace officer license or certification revoked or surrendered.

headings.title: Discretionary probation or denial and written notice
headings.reviewNote: Provides that when cause exists, the director may grant the application subject to probation or deny it, and requires written notice of reasons and appeal rights.

headings.title: Thirty-day AHC appeal and waiver upon untimeliness
headings.reviewNote: Allows an aggrieved applicant to appeal within thirty days to the AHC to determine cause (barring AHC consideration of severity or rehabilitation), with failure to request a hearing within thirty days waiving appeal.

headings.title: Director thirty-day disposition hearing after cause finding
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director, unbound by prior action, to hold a hearing within thirty days of an AHC cause finding to determine probation or denial, with nonappearance waiving the hearing.

headings.title: Application of chapter 621 administrative procedures
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 621 and its amendments, except where conflicting with chapter 590, to AHC proceedings under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections of 590.100 (2026 H.B. 1866); corrected subsection 2 from mandatory denial to cause for denial (matching subsection 3 discretion).

headings.title: Definitions for peer support counseling
headings.reviewNote: Defines eight terms including emergency services personnel/provider, employee assistance program, law enforcement agency/personnel, peer support counseling session, peer support specialist, and peer support team.

headings.title: Confidentiality of peer support session communications
headings.reviewNote: Declares communications made by a participant or peer support specialist and oral or written information conveyed in or as a result of a session confidential and not subject to disclosure by any participant.

headings.title: Confidentiality of specialist and EAP staff communications
headings.reviewNote: Declares session-related communications among peer support specialists and employee assistance program supervisors or staff confidential and not subject to disclosure.

headings.title: Limitation to sessions conducted by peer support specialists
headings.reviewNote: Restricts the section's application strictly to peer support counseling sessions conducted by a peer support specialist.

headings.title: Chapter 610 exemption and preservation of independent employment evidence
headings.reviewNote: Applies confidentiality to all session oral communications, notes, records, and reports, exempts them from chapter 610 public records, and preserves discovery or admissibility of independent employment observations and materials.

headings.title: Five exceptions to peer counseling confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Excludes threats of suicide or criminal acts, spouse/child/elder abuse or mandatory-reporting information, admissions of criminal conduct, and expressly consented testimony by a participant or deceased participant's surviving spouse or estate representative.

headings.title: Permitted communications among specialists and EAP staff
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not prohibit communications among peer support specialists or between specialists and employee assistance program supervisors or staff.

headings.title: Permitted fitness-for-duty communications with employer
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not prohibit communications regarding employee fitness for duty between an employee assistance program and an employer.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections of 590.1040 (2018 H.B. 1355 merged with S.B. 870); corrected subsection 7 from misplaced independent-evidence text to permitted specialist/EAP communications.

headings.title: Peace officer basic training tuition reimbursement program established
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Peace Officer Basic Training Tuition Reimbursement Program within DPS for appropriated reimbursements to qualifying Missouri residents and government entities paying basic training tuition.

headings.title: Administrative duties of POST commission
headings.reviewNote: Designates the POST commission as administrative agency to prescribe forms, timing, and methods, select qualifying recipients, and determine payment manner.

headings.title: Individual peace officer eligibility requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires initial employment on or after September 1, 2023, initial and annual applications with employer verification, transcript, and tuition statement, and at least one year of current full-time Missouri peace officer employment.

headings.title: Government entity eligibility requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires employing an officer initially employed on or after September 1, 2023, submitting initial and annual applications (up to four years) with verification, transcript, and tuition/fees statement, and certifying at least one year of full-time employment.

headings.title: Four-year twenty-five-percent annual reimbursement schedule
headings.reviewNote: Provides subject to fund availability for 25% tuition reimbursement after each of years one through four of continuous full-time employment, allowing a government entity to qualify even if the officer moves to another Missouri agency.

headings.title: Six-thousand-dollar maximum reimbursement per officer
headings.reviewNote: Caps total tuition reimbursement under this section at $6,000 per eligible person or employee.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS to promulgate administrative rules under chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability voiding post-August 28, 2023 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 590.1070; removed fabricated annual programmatic cap from subsection 6 and added September 1, 2023 eligibility dates and August 28, 2023 nonseverability clause.

headings.title: Director investigation, inspection, and subpoena powers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to investigate disciplinary or denial causes, inspect training centers, and subpoena witnesses for sworn depositions and relevant documents or sworn copies.

headings.title: Circuit court show-cause enforcement of subpoenas
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to apply to the Cole County circuit court or the circuit court where the person resides or is found for a show-cause order and civil enforcement of disobeyed subpoenas.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 590.110; aligned subpoena issuance in subsection 1 and circuit court show-cause enforcement in subsection 2.

headings.title: Availability of completed investigations to hiring agencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires making all completed investigations of alleged peace officer acts available to any hiring law enforcement agency without making transferred records public records.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of unfitness for licensure to POST commission
headings.reviewNote: Requires any law enforcement agency possessing information showing a peace officer's unfitness for licensure to provide that information to the POST commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 590.118 (2004 S.B. 1211); replaced fabricated state funding forfeiture in subsection 2 with mandatory reporting of unfitness to POST.

headings.title: Creation, eleven-member composition, and qualifications of POST commission
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the 11-member POST commission within DPS appointed by the governor with senate consent from the director's list, specifying law enforcement and public member representation, congressional district limits, residency, and a one-year reappointment wait.

headings.title: Staggered terms, removal by director, vacancies, and agency limit
headings.reviewNote: Sets staggered three-year terms, authorizes removal by the director for misconduct, neglect, or cause (with written reasons and requested hearing), fills vacancies for unexpired terms, and bars two members from the same agency.

headings.title: Chairperson appointment by director, semi-annual meetings, and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to annually appoint a chairperson, mandates at least two meetings per year, and sets a majority quorum.

headings.title: Prohibition on member compensation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no member of the POST commission shall receive any compensation for performing official duties.

headings.title: Advisory duty of POST commission to director
headings.reviewNote: Directs the POST commission to guide and advise the director concerning chapter duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 590.120; realigned shifted subsections 2-5 and corrected removal/chairperson authority (director, not governor) and meeting frequency (at least twice yearly, not quarterly).

headings.title: Citation as Police Use of Force Transparency Act of 2021
headings.reviewNote: Designates the section as the Police Use of Force Transparency Act of 2021.

headings.title: Definitions of use-of-force reporting terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines law enforcement agency, peace officer, serious physical injury (section 556.061), and use-of-force incident (fatality, serious bodily injury, or firearm discharge at or toward a person).

headings.title: Annual agency reporting to FBI database starting March 1, 2022
headings.reviewNote: Requires each law enforcement agency, starting March 1, 2022, and at least annually thereafter, to report local use-of-force data to the FBI National Use of Force Data Collection without officer personally identifying information.

headings.title: Concurrent agency reporting to department of public safety
headings.reviewNote: Requires each law enforcement agency to report its subsection 3 data to DPS without personally identifying information of individual officers.

headings.title: Department data standards deadline of October 31, 2021
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS, no later than October 31, 2021, to develop data collection and reporting standards consistent with the FBI National Use of Force Data Collection.

headings.title: Annual public website publication starting March 1, 2023
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS, by March 1, 2023, and at least annually thereafter, to publish statewide aggregate and agency-specific data on its website as a chapter 610 public record.

headings.title: Public trends and disparities analysis report by June 30, 2025
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS to release a public analysis of use-of-force trends and disparities by June 30, 2025, updated at least once every five years.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 590.1265:50165 (2021 S.B. 53 & 60; dual version printed with S.B. 26 due to possible conflict); corrected subsection 7 from annual legislative report to public report by June 30, 2025 updated every 5 years.

headings.title: Citation as Police Use of Force Transparency Act of 2021
headings.reviewNote: Designates the section as the Police Use of Force Transparency Act of 2021.

headings.title: Definitions of use-of-force reporting terms
headings.reviewNote: Defines law enforcement agency, peace officer, and use-of-force incident (fatality, serious bodily injury, or firearm discharge at or toward a person).

headings.title: Annual agency reporting to FBI database
headings.reviewNote: Requires each law enforcement agency, at least annually, to collect and report local use-of-force data to the FBI National Use of Force Data Collection.

headings.title: Concurrent agency reporting to department of public safety
headings.reviewNote: Requires each law enforcement agency to report its subsection 3 data to DPS without personally identifying information of individual officers.

headings.title: Department data standards deadline of June 30, 2022
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS, no later than June 30, 2022, to develop data collection and reporting standards consistent with the FBI National Use of Force Data Collection.

headings.title: Public report of statewide and agency-specific data
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS to publish reported statewide aggregate and agency-specific data in a publicly available report deemed a chapter 610 public record.

headings.title: Public trends and disparities analysis report by January 1, 2025
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS to release a public analysis of use-of-force trends and disparities by January 1, 2025, updated at least once every five years.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 590.1265:50096 (2021 S.B. 26; dual version printed with S.B. 53 & 60 due to possible conflict); corrected subsection 7 from annual legislative report to public report by January 1, 2025 updated every 5 years.

headings.title: Missouri Rangers school crisis training program established
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to establish the Missouri Rangers training program and minimum standards for instructors, centers, and programs focused on preventing and responding to school emergencies or violent crises.

headings.title: Background check, physical fitness test, and military discharge rule
headings.reviewNote: Requires FBI criminal history background checks forwarded to the designating agency, age-tiered physical fitness tests prior to entry, and honorable discharge for former or retired military applicants.

headings.title: Limited arrest powers and active officer exemption
headings.reviewNote: Limits Missouri ranger arrest powers to actively employed rangers on school/district property or school buses for chapter 571 and section 569.140/569.155 offenses involving school property, exempting active law enforcement officers.

headings.title: One-hundred-sixty-hour curriculum and abbreviated veteran program
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to develop an up-to-160-hour curriculum covering enumerated crisis, legal, firearms, and first-aid topics, plus an abbreviated program for active/retired law enforcement (10+ years) or military/National Guard.

headings.title: Continuing education rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to promulgate continuing education rules under chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability voiding post-August 28, 2026 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Discretionary part-time training program
headings.reviewNote: Provides that POST may develop a part-time training program satisfying all section requirements.

headings.title: Certificate of completion issued by approved instructor
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an approved Missouri ranger training instructor may issue a completion certificate affirming passage and must provide a copy to the director of public safety.

headings.title: Issuance of certificate and Missouri ranger badge
headings.reviewNote: Requires each person who successfully completes the training program to receive a certificate and a Missouri ranger badge.

headings.title: Uniform outer garment RANGER lettering requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the front and back of the outermost garment of the ranger uniform to display capitalized block letters spelling 'RANGER'.

headings.title: School board weapon authorization and level three holster
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rangers to carry firearms or lethal weapons on school property or buses if approved by the hiring school/district (which decides carrying, weapon type, and concealment), and requires a level three retention holster for open-carried pistols.

headings.title: School employee status for liability, optional benefits, and immunity
headings.reviewNote: Deems rangers school/district employees solely for liability and workers' compensation (archived footnote notes 'purposes' in original S.B. 905 rolls), allows optional benefits and full-time/part-time/volunteer status, and applies qualified immunity and the public duty rule.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 11 subsections of 590.1300 (2026 S.B. 905 merged with S.B. 1421); removed fabricated drug testing/ID card details, added abbreviated program and active-officer exemption, and noted the S.B. 905 roll footnote.

headings.title: Creation, administration, and interest of POST commission fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Peace Officer Standards and Training Commission Fund in the state treasury, administered by POST solely for required training under sections 590.100 to 590.180 or commission-approved training, with earned interest credited to the fund.

headings.title: Nonreversion of fund balances to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Exempts moneys in the fund from transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 590.178; verified alignment and added interest-crediting detail in subsection 1.

headings.title: Arrest validity independent of officer licensure status
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits deeming an arrest unlawful solely due to peace officer licensure status and bars receiving evidence on the question in any civil or criminal case.

headings.title: Open and confidential status of officer licensing records
headings.reviewNote: Makes applicant/licensee name, licensure status, and agency an open record while keeping other director-retained records confidential (with consent, interstate exchange, litigation, state agency, and final-discipline exceptions) and preserving closed-record and attorney-client/work-product privileges.

headings.title: Discovery and admissibility of records in chapter proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Makes applicant/licensee records discoverable by the director and admissible in chapter proceedings regardless of open/closed status or privilege, except attorney-client privilege.

headings.title: Good-faith, non-negligent immunity for submitting information
headings.reviewNote: Grants criminal and civil immunity to persons or entities submitting information to the director under chapter 590 in good faith and without negligence.

headings.title: Prohibition against unauthorized use of testing materials
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unauthorized use of testing materials or certification examinations administered under section 590.030(2).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 590.180; added attorney-client privilege exception in subsection 3 and without-negligence requirement in subsection 4.

headings.title: Critical incident stress management program and definitions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Critical Incident Stress Management Program within DPS for peace officers and first responders, authorizes crisis intervention services, and defines critical incident and first responder.

headings.title: Mandatory mental health check-in every three to five years
headings.reviewNote: Requires peace officers and first responders to complete a check-in with a program provider (or qualifying department behavioral health program) every three to five years, with completion notice sent to their commanding officer, director, or supervisor.

headings.title: Privilege for program disclosures and three exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Declares disclosed information privileged and inadmissible in criminal, administrative, or civil proceedings against the officer or first responder unless necessary to prevent harm, consented in writing, or required under mandatory reporting laws.

headings.title: 988 Public Safety Fund, rulemaking, nonreversion, and investment
headings.reviewNote: Creates the dedicated 988 Public Safety Fund in the state treasury with nonreversion under section 33.080, interest crediting, and permissive director rulemaking subject to chapter 536 nonseverability (voiding post-August 28, 2021 rules if review powers are held unconstitutional).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 590.192 (2026 H.B. 2372 merged with H.B. 2637 & 3155 merged with S.B. 975); verified alignment and added supervisor-notice and August 28, 2021 nonseverability details.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor for unlicensed commission or commissioning
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly holding a peace officer commission without a valid license, or granting or continuing such a commission, as a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor for purposeful chapter violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies purposely violating any other provision of chapter 590 as a class B misdemeanor.

headings.title: Ineligibility of violating agencies for state or federal funds
headings.reviewNote: Renders any law enforcement agency commissioning an officer in violation of chapter 590 or otherwise violating the chapter ineligible for state or federal law enforcement, safety, training, or criminal justice funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 590.195; corrected misdemeanor class from class A to class B in subsections 1-2 and replaced fabricated injunctive-action heading in subsection 3 with agency funding ineligibility.

headings.title: POST commission duties for school protection officer training
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to establish minimum training standards, minimum training hours, and curriculum for school protection officers.

headings.title: Minimum required school protection officer training topics
headings.reviewNote: Requires training at a minimum to cover school violence prevention, emergency/violent crisis handling, state criminal law review, defensive force, deadly force, and self-defense spray devices.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 590.200 (2014 S.B. 656 veto override effective 10-10-14); replaced fabricated approved-centers heading in subsection 2 with the six minimum required curriculum topics.

headings.title: Minimum standards for school protection officer training
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to establish minimum standards for school protection officer training instructors, training centers, and training programs.

headings.title: Director approved list and POST-certified firearms instructor requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to maintain and share with school districts an approved list meeting section 590.200 and 590.205 standards, and requires training by firearms instructors who completed a POST-certified law enforcement firearms instructor school.

headings.title: Fingerprint card and FBI background check for applicants
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to submit a fingerprint card and FBI background check authorization to the training center or program, which forwards the report to the designating school district.

headings.title: Valid concealed carry endorsement or permit required for admission
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits admitting any person to a school protection officer training center or program without proof of a valid concealed carry endorsement or permit.

headings.title: Certificate of completion issued by approved instructor
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an approved instructor may issue a completion certificate affirming passage and indicating concealed carry permit status, with a copy provided to the director of public safety.

headings.title: Continuing education and twenty-hour annual firearms training
headings.reviewNote: Requires POST to establish continuing education requirements and mandates twenty hours of annual firearms skill development training for all school protection officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections of 590.205 (2026 H.B. 1866); realigned shifted subsections 4-6 to capture the concealed carry admission prerequisite, instructor-issued certificates, and 20-hour annual firearms training.

headings.title: Establishment of Committee on School Safety
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Committee on School Safety within the department of public safety.

headings.title: Committee membership and organizational representation
headings.reviewNote: Specifies membership: up to three DPS representatives and one representative each from the Missouri Sheriff's Association, Missouri Municipal League, DESE, and MSBA Center for Education Safety.

headings.title: Designation of department representative as chair
headings.reviewNote: Requires one member representing the department of public safety to serve as chair of the committee.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and optional expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that committee members serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for actual necessary official expenses.

headings.title: Quarterly meeting schedule and school safety guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires meeting at least four times per year and at least once per calendar quarter to evaluate and establish school safety guidelines, including school firearm violence prevention plans.

headings.title: Open meetings subject to section 610.021 exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires all committee meetings to be open to the public except as provided in section 610.021.

headings.title: Annual written report to governor and legislative leaders
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting an annual written report to the governor, senate president pro tempore, and house speaker.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 590.208 (2025 H.B. 495); corrected fabricated membership in subsection 2, replaced fabricated terms/election in subsection 3 with DPS chair designation, and added section 610.021 exception in subsection 6.

headings.title: Definitions for officer administrative investigations
headings.reviewNote: Defines administering authority, color of law, economic loss, good cause, and law enforcement officer (excluding the highest ranking officer in the agency).

headings.title: Conditions and timelines for administrative investigations and questioning
headings.reviewNote: Sets fourteen mandatory conditions for administrative investigations or questioning, including 24-hour written notice and complaint copy, confidential complainant ID, on-duty/secure-location interviews, Garrity advisements, counsel/representation, 90-day investigation deadline with extensions/tolling, 5-day findings notice, record copy, and chapter 610 confidentiality.

headings.title: Full due process hearing rights and minimum components
headings.reviewNote: Entitles officers facing unpaid suspension, demotion, termination, transfer, or economic-loss status to a due process hearing with representation, 7-day notice and document access, right to refuse testimony during concurrent criminal charges, appeal record, and chapter 610 confidentiality (allowing more favorable bargaining agreements).

headings.title: Written decision, findings of fact, and prompt delivery
headings.reviewNote: Requires post-hearing decisions or actions to be in writing with concise findings of fact on each issue, delivered or mailed promptly with right-of-appeal notice.

headings.title: Right to attach written response to adverse personnel material
headings.reviewNote: Gives officers the opportunity to provide a written response permanently attached to any adverse material placed in their personnel file.

headings.title: Compensation for economic loss upon finding of no misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Entitles officers to compensation for economic loss incurred during an investigation if found to have committed no misconduct.

headings.title: Employer defense and indemnification with criminal-conviction exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires employers to defend and indemnify officers for official-duty and off-duty color-of-law civil claims, ending the obligation upon criminal conviction or guilty plea arising from the same conduct.

headings.title: Protection against discipline for asserting constitutional rights
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits disciplining, demoting, dismissing, transferring, or causing economic loss to an officer for asserting constitutional rights in a judicial proceeding unless the officer admits wrongdoing.

headings.title: Circuit court judicial enforcement actions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes aggrieved officers or authorized representatives to bring enforcement suits in the circuit court where the agency or governmental body has its principal place of business.

headings.title: Voiding of violating actions, discretionary fees, and one-year limit
headings.reviewNote: Requires courts, upon preponderance-of-the-evidence proof of a violation, to void violating actions, authorizes awarding costs and attorneys' fees, and sets a one-year filing limit from when the violation is ascertainable.

headings.title: Inapplicability to director licensing actions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts any investigation or other action by the director regarding a chapter 590 license from this section.

headings.title: Compliance through substantially similar or greater procedures
headings.reviewNote: Deems a law enforcement agency with substantially similar or greater procedures to be in compliance with this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 12 subsections of 590.502; corrected subsection 1 definitions, 7-day (not 30-day) hearing notice in subsection 3, removed fabricated 30-day limit in subsection 5, corrected subsection 8 to constitutional rights, and replaced fabricated $5,000 civil penalty in subsection 10 with voiding/fees/1-year limit.

headings.title: Definition of minority group
headings.reviewNote: Defines minority group as individuals of African, Hispanic, Native American, or Asian descent.

headings.title: Officer reporting of motor vehicle stop data
headings.reviewNote: Requires peace officers to report ten enumerated categories of demographic, reason, search, contraband, citation/arrest, and location data for each motor vehicle stop, using a DPS-determined format.

headings.title: Annual agency compilation and March first attorney general report
headings.reviewNote: Requires each law enforcement agency to compile calendar-year stop data and submit a report to the attorney general by March first in the attorney general's format.

headings.title: Attorney general annual analysis and June first report
headings.reviewNote: Requires the attorney general to analyze agency reports and submit findings (including four required agency metrics) to the governor, general assembly, and each agency by June first.

headings.title: Mandatory agency policy on race-based traffic stops
headings.reviewNote: Requires each agency to adopt a policy prohibiting pretextual race-based stops, periodically reviewing the attorney general's report for disproportionate patterns, investigating patterns, and providing counseling and training within ninety days.

headings.title: Discretionary withholding of state funds for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the governor may withhold state funds appropriated to a noncompliant law enforcement agency.

headings.title: Permissive use of federal funds for vehicle audio-video equipment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that law enforcement agencies may use federal COPS grants or other federal funds to equip traffic-stop vehicles with video cameras and voice-activated microphones.

headings.title: Exemption for lawful sobriety checkpoints or roadblocks
headings.reviewNote: Exempts officers stopping drivers at lawfully conducted sobriety checkpoints or roadblocks from subsection 2 reporting.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections of 590.650; added June first deadline and recipients in subsection 4, corrected subsection 5 policy components, and fixed duplicate-word typo in subsection 8.

headings.title: Local authority to establish civilian review or oversight entities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes cities, counties, and St. Louis City to establish or use a local-body-appointed civilian review board or oversight entity to investigate public misconduct allegations, with uncompensated members reimbursed for reasonable necessary expenses.

headings.title: Limited complaint-recommendation powers and express preemption
headings.reviewNote: Limits entity powers solely to receiving, investigating, making findings, and recommending discipline to the chief law enforcement official on specified misconduct complaints, bars relying solely on unsworn or prior unsubstantiated/unfounded/withdrawn complaints, and preempts and voids all authority outside listed powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 590.653 (2024 S.B. 754, et al.); added evidentiary limits and express preemption in subsection 2.

headings.title: Definitions of custodial interrogation and recording
headings.reviewNote: Defines custodial interrogation (with five exclusions including voluntary meetings, non-arrest detentions, routine processing, alcohol influence reports, and transport) and recorded/recording.

headings.title: Mandatory recording when feasible for enumerated serious felonies
headings.reviewNote: Requires recording, when feasible, all custodial interrogations of persons suspected of committing or attempting eighteen enumerated homicide, assault, elder/child abuse, robbery, arson, sexual, and kidnapping offenses.

headings.title: Discretionary recording and six exceptions to mandatory recording
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes recording in any circumstance with or without suspect knowledge or consent, and lists six exceptions where subsection 2 recording is not required (suspect request, out-of-state, exigent safety, spontaneous statements, equipment failure, or unavailable equipment).

headings.title: Mandatory written agency recording policy
headings.reviewNote: Requires each law enforcement agency to adopt a written policy to record custodial interrogations for subsection 2 felonies.

headings.title: Discretionary withholding of state funds absent good faith
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the governor may withhold state funds from a noncompliant agency if the governor finds the agency did not act in good faith in attempting to comply.

headings.title: No evidence exclusion or trial reference to compliance
headings.reviewNote: Bars using the section to exclude evidence, limits violation impact to subsection 5, and prohibits admitting, arguing, referencing, considering, or questioning compliance or noncompliance at criminal trial.

headings.title: No private cause of action created
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in the section authorizes, creates, or implies a private cause of action.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 7 subsections of 590.700; corrected subsection 1 definitions (recorded/recording, not place of detention), added the six exceptions in subsection 3, and added the good-faith condition in subsection 5.

headings.title: Sole department authority to regulate corporate security advisors
headings.reviewNote: Grants DPS sole authority to regulate and license corporate security advisors and denies arrest powers for criminal code violations to licensed advisors who are not also department-commissioned, except as otherwise provided by law.

headings.title: Sole commissioning authority, peace officer license, and oath
headings.reviewNote: Grants the director sole commissioning authority, requires a valid peace officer license, and requires subscribing the Article VII, Section 11 constitutional oath before a circuit clerk and filing it with the director.

headings.title: Statewide geographical jurisdiction and reciprocity exception
headings.reviewNote: Limits corporate security advisor authority and jurisdiction only by state boundaries unless the license is recognized by another state or federal law or regulation.

headings.title: Employer minimum liability insurance and named-insured statement
headings.reviewNote: Requires DPS to set minimum employer liability insurance and obtain an employer statement naming the corporate security advisor as a named insured.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for acting without a license
headings.reviewNote: Classifies acting as a corporate security advisor without a DPS license as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Permissive director rulemaking under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the director may promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 and section 590.190.

headings.title: Grandfather clause for advisors licensed as of February 1, 2014
headings.reviewNote: Exempts corporate security advisors licensed as of February 1, 2014, from applying for a new department license until expiration or revocation.

headings.title: Application forms and licensing fee up to two hundred dollars
headings.reviewNote: Requires applications on director-prescribed forms and requires DPS to charge a license issuance fee up to $200 set by chapter 536 regulation.

headings.title: No sovereign immunity waiver and department civil immunity
headings.reviewNote: Preserves state sovereign immunity without creating state liability and grants DPS and the director civil immunity arising from commissioning corporate security advisors.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 9 subsections of 590.750 (2015 H.B. 878 veto override effective 10-16-15); verified alignment and preserved reciprocity and permissive rulemaking nuances.

headings.title: Prohibition on respiratory choke-holds with defense exception
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a law enforcement officer from knowingly using a respiratory choke-hold unless in defense of the officer or another from serious physical injury or death.

headings.title: Definition of respiratory choke-hold
headings.reviewNote: Defines respiratory choke-hold to include using any body part or object to attempt to control or disable by applying pressure to a person's neck with the purpose of controlling or restricting breathing.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 590.805; verified alignment with archived source text.
